title: Trivial upper bound on deterministic communication complexity
statement:
Let $X$ and $\alpha$ be finite nonempty types, let $Y$ be an arbitrary type, and let $f : X \to Y \to \alpha$ be a two-argument function. Then the deterministic communication complexity of $f$ satisfies
\[
  D(f) \;\le\; \lceil \log_2 \abs{X} \rceil + \lceil \log_2 \abs{\alpha} \rceil,
\]
where $\abs{X}$ and $\abs{\alpha}$ denote the cardinalities of $X$ and $\alpha$.
hypotheses_covered: f : X → Y → α a two-argument function
replaced:
For finite, nonempty types $X$ and $\alpha$ and any function $f : X \to Y \to \alpha$,
the deterministic communication complexity satisfies
\[
  \mathrm{CC}(f) \;\le\; \lceil\log_2 |X|\rceil + \lceil\log_2 |\alpha|\rceil.
\]
This bound is achieved by the protocol in which Alice sends her input $x$ to Bob,
and Bob computes and sends back the output $f(x, y)$.
